text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning.Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- Cyprus-registered Mustcom consortium won a 25 percent plus one stake in Russia's telecoms holding company Svyazinvest on Friday in Moscow's biggest privatisation auction that will bring the government $1.875 billion. The consortium is backed by Russia's giant Uneximbank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the London-based investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank.
- Russia's space officials are not planning to shut down the crippled Mir station and expect to raise about $100 billion to carry out necessary but risky repairs.
- The State Tax Service is planning to tighten control over collecting money from alcohol industry debtors, the head of the service, Alexander Pochinok, is quoted as saying.
SEVODNYA

- A 47-year-old film director armed with a crossbow shot arrows at the Kremlin on Friday to draw attention to the pitiful state of Russia's film industry and to protest against the strong influence of Western films on the Russian market.
- President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree imposing a 0.5 percent tax on every operation to buy hard currency. Russian banks have sold about 12.5 billion dollars in cash in the last six months.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- The haste with which reforms started in the army has been caused by the extreme tension among servicemen. Urgent steps to pay off wage arrears to the military are aimed at appeasing their anger and keeping them out of politics, says the paper.

- Russia is considering measures to respond to anti-dumping restrictions towards Russian exporters, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov is quoted as saying. At the same time the paper raps some politicians for hampering the process of integration with European markets.
IZVESTIA

- Patriarch Alexiy, head of the Russian Orthodox Church, criticised President Boris Yeltsin for the first time in public for vetoing a controversial law on religion. The bill stirred fears among human right groups and religious minorities that Russia was returning to Soviet-style control of worship.

- Russia's economy is recovering and structural reforms of natural monopolies are under way, said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Friday, reporting on the government's economic achievements over the last six months.
- Over one million Russians were in prison on July 1, according to an Interior Ministry report.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- President Boris Yeltsin said in his radio address on Friday that he vetoed the law on religion because it violated human rights.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The government is planning to find new sources of budget revenues, the head of the State Tax Service Alexander Pochinok is quoted as saying.
KOMSOMOLSKAY PRAVDA

- The paper raises the problem of psychological compatibility of cosmonauts during long space flights and reveals a number of difficulties the international crews have been facing on the Mir space station.
- Russia's mass media giant "Dom Kommersant", which publishes major business newspapers and magazines, is likely to change its owner, the paper says.
TRUD
- Russian film director Yuri Karo is planning to shoot a feature film on the troubled Mir space station, expecting to spend about $12 million on the project.
--Tatyana Ustonova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
